— Pertussis toxin (PTX) catalyzes ADP-ribosylation of the Gα_{i/o} subunit at a conserved cysteine residue, covalently locking it in a conformation that cannot undergo receptor-catalyzed GDP→GTP exchange, thereby preventing activation of any G_{i/o}-coupled receptor signaling. This state is encoded as G_{i/o}^{blocked}.

— H-89 is a selective PKA inhibitor that directly blocks PKA catalytic activity by occupying the ATP-binding site of the PKA catalytic subunit. Its action is cAMP-independent: it abolishes PKA kinase activity regardless of intracellular cAMP concentration and does not affect any upstream node (G proteins, adenylyl cyclase, or cAMP synthesis). Its state is encoded as PKA^{blocked}.

— IBMX is a non-selective phosphodiesterase (PDE) inhibitor that blocks the enzymatic hydrolysis of cAMP to 5′-AMP by PDEs, thereby preventing cAMP degradation. IBMX acts strictly at the level of cAMP degradation and does not affect G proteins, adenylyl cyclase, PKA, or any node downstream of cAMP. Its mechanistic state is encoded as the single node IBMX, and its consequence on the cAMP pool — when combined with unrestrained AC activity — is encoded as Δ[cAMP]^{max}.

— Prostacyclin acts at the IP receptor (a G_s-coupled receptor), encoded as Activation(R_{Gs}), which activates G_s (encoded as G_s^{+}) and drives AC stimulation.

The two upstream branches — one originating from PTX and one from Activation(R_{Gs}) — converge at a shared AC node; use the notation [A ∥ B] → C to represent this convergence. Use only the allowed symbols: Activation(R_{Gs}), G_s^{+}, PTX, G_{i/o}^{blocked}, AC^{+}, AC^{++}, Δ[cAMP] > 0, IBMX, Δ[cAMP]^{max}, H-89, PKA^{blocked}, Exocytosis^{+}, Exocytosis^{-}.

Express the complete signaling chain for this four-way perturbation condition as a single left-to-right arrow chain wrapped in $\boxed{\cdots}$.
output:
## 解答

**S1 — Reproduce the triple-perturbation scaffold (sub_prev)**

From the previous step, the established chain is:

PTX → G_{i/o}^{blocked} → AC^{+} → Δ[cAMP] > 0 → IBMX → Δ[cAMP]^{max} → H-89 → PKA^{blocked} → Exocytosis^{+}

Mechanism summary:
- PTX ADP-ribosylates Gα_{i/o} → G_{i/o}^{blocked}: tonic G_{i/o}-mediated AC inhibition is removed → AC^{+}.
- AC^{+} drives cAMP accumulation → Δ[cAMP] > 0.
- IBMX blocks PDE-mediated cAMP hydrolysis → cAMP reaches ceiling → Δ[cAMP]^{max}.
- H-89 occupies PKA catalytic ATP-binding site cAMP-independently → PKA^{blocked}.
- PKA^{blocked} removes inhibitory phosphorylation on SNARE/VASP components → Exocytosis^{+}.

**S2 — Introduce the G_s-coupled agonist branch**

Prostacyclin (IP receptor agonist) activates the G_s-coupled IP receptor:

Activation(R_{Gs}) → G_s^{+}

Gα_s directly stimulates adenylyl cyclase at its catalytic/stimulatory regulatory site.

**S3 — Determine additivity vs. redundancy at the AC node**

The PTX branch removes G_{i/o}-mediated *inhibition* of AC (a disinhibition mechanism, acting at the inhibitory regulatory site of AC). The G_s branch provides *direct positive stimulation* of AC via Gα_s (acting at the stimulatory regulatory site of AC). These two inputs act through mechanistically distinct sites on AC and are therefore *additive*, not redundant.

Merged AC state: AC^{++} (doubly activated: G_{i/o}-inhibition removed AND G_s direct stimulation added). AC^{++} > AC^{+} in catalytic activity.

The two upstream branches converge at AC^{++}:
[PTX → G_{i/o}^{blocked} → AC^{+}] ∥ [Activation(R_{Gs}) → G_s^{+}] → AC^{++}

**S4 — Propagate downstream from AC^{++}**

- AC^{++} → Δ[cAMP] > 0: cAMP synthesis is elevated (faster rate than AC^{+} alone), initiating accumulation.
- IBMX → Δ[cAMP]^{max}: PDE hydrolysis is fully blocked. The terminal cAMP node symbol remains Δ[cAMP]^{max} because this encodes the ceiling state (synthesis unrestrained, degradation fully blocked). AC^{++} accelerates the rate of reaching Δ[cAMP]^{max} but does not alter the encoded node symbol.
- H-89 → PKA^{blocked}: H-89 acts cAMP-independently at the PKA catalytic subunit. Even Δ[cAMP]^{max} cannot displace H-89 from its binding site. PKA^{blocked} is unchanged.
- PKA^{blocked} → Exocytosis^{+}: Absence of PKA-mediated inhibitory phosphorylation on SNARE/VASP components disinhibits granule exocytosis. Exocytosis^{+} is unchanged.

**S5 — Assemble the complete extended chain**

The full chain, with the single new convergence node AC^{++} introduced at the merge point:

[PTX → G_{i/o}^{blocked} → AC^{+}] ∥ [Activation(R_{Gs}) → G_s^{+}] → AC^{++} → Δ[cAMP] > 0 → IBMX → Δ[cAMP]^{max} → H-89 → PKA^{blocked} → Exocytosis^{+}

Exactly one new convergence node (AC^{++}) and one new upstream branch (Activation(R_{Gs}) → G_s^{+}) have been added. All nodes from Δ[cAMP] > 0 onward are inherited unchanged from the triple-perturbation scaffold.

最终答案：\boxed{[\text{PTX} \to G_{i/o}^{\text{blocked}} \to AC^{+}] \parallel [\text{Activation}(R_{Gs}) \to G_s^{+}] \to AC^{++} \to \Delta[\text{cAMP}] > 0 \to \text{IBMX} \to \Delta[\text{cAMP}]^{\max} \to \text{H-89} \to PKA^{\text{blocked}} \to \text{Exocytosis}^{+}}

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
Platelets express G_{i/o}-coupled opioid receptors whose activation suppresses adenylyl cyclase (AC), lowers cAMP, inactivates PKA, and thereby disinhibits granule exocytosis. Three pharmacological agents are applied simultaneously to platelets:

• Pertussis toxin (PTX) catalyzes ADP-ribosylation of the Gα_{i/o} subunit at a conserved cysteine residue, covalently locking it in a conformation that cannot undergo receptor-catalyzed GDP→GTP exchange, thereby preventing activation of any G_{i/o}-coupled receptor signaling. This state is encoded as the single node G_{i/o}^{\text{blocked}}.

• H-89 is a selective PKA inhibitor that directly blocks PKA catalytic activity by occupying the ATP-binding site of the PKA catalytic subunit. Its action is cAMP-independent: it abolishes PKA kinase activity regardless of intracellular cAMP concentration and does not affect any upstream node (G proteins, adenylyl cyclase, or cAMP synthesis). Its state is encoded as PKA^{\text{blocked}}.

• IBMX is a non-selective phosphodiesterase (PDE) inhibitor that blocks the enzymatic hydrolysis of cAMP to 5′-AMP by PDEs, thereby preventing cAMP degradation. IBMX acts strictly at the level of cAMP degradation and does not affect G proteins, adenylyl cyclase, PKA, or any node downstream of cAMP. Its mechanistic state is encoded as the single node IBMX, and its consequence on the cAMP pool — when combined with unrestrained AC activity — is encoded as Δ[cAMP]^{\max} (cAMP maximally elevated: synthesis unrestrained and degradation blocked).

Using only the allowed symbols $\{\text{PTX},\; G_{i/o}^{\text{blocked}},\; AC^{+},\; \Delta[\text{cAMP}] > 0,\; \text{IBMX},\; \Delta[\text{cAMP}]^{\max},\; \text{H-89},\; PKA^{\text{blocked}},\; \text{Exocytosis}^{+},\; \text{Exocytosis}^{-}\}$ and left-to-right arrow-chain notation, derive the complete signaling chain for the PTX + IBMX + H-89 triple-perturbation condition in platelets, starting from PTX and terminating with the exocytosis state.

Express your final answer as a single arrow chain wrapped in $\boxed{\cdots}$, using only the allowed symbols listed above.
output:
## 解答

S1 (Reconstruct double-perturbation scaffold from prior step):
The PTX + H-89 chain established previously is:
PTX → G_{i/o}^{blocked} → AC^{+} → Δ[cAMP] > 0 → H-89 → PKA^{blocked} → Exocytosis^{+}.
This serves as the upstream scaffold into which the single new node is inserted.

S2 (Identify insertion point for IBMX):
IBMX is a non-selective PDE inhibitor. Its mechanistic action is to block the hydrolysis of cAMP to 5′-AMP by phosphodiesterases. This action operates strictly at the level of cAMP degradation — it does not touch G proteins, adenylyl cyclase, PKA, or any downstream effector. Therefore, IBMX must be inserted at the cAMP node, between the position where cAMP has begun to accumulate (Δ[cAMP] > 0, produced by AC^{+} after PTX removes G_{i/o}-mediated inhibition) and the next downstream node (H-89).

S3 (Derive the consequence of IBMX on the cAMP pool):
Prior to IBMX: PTX has already blocked G_{i/o}, so AC is disinhibited (AC^{+}) and is producing cAMP — yielding Δ[cAMP] > 0.
After IBMX: PDE-mediated cAMP hydrolysis is now also blocked. With both synthesis unrestrained (AC^{+}) and degradation abolished (IBMX), the cAMP pool reaches a maximal level. This state is encoded as Δ[cAMP]^{max}. The intermediate causal sequence is therefore: Δ[cAMP] > 0 → IBMX → Δ[cAMP]^{max}.

S4 (Propagate through H-89 to PKA and exocytosis):
Despite Δ[cAMP]^{max}, H-89 occupies the ATP-binding site of the PKA catalytic subunit in a cAMP-independent manner. The elevated cAMP cannot rescue PKA activity because H-89's inhibition is upstream of cAMP-dependent conformational activation at the catalytic site. Therefore, PKA^{blocked} is unchanged: Δ[cAMP]^{max} → H-89 → PKA^{blocked}.
With PKA^{blocked}, no inhibitory phosphorylation is imposed on SNARE components or VASP, so granule exocytosis remains disinhibited: PKA^{blocked} → Exocytosis^{+}.

S5 (Assemble complete triple-perturbation chain):
Concatenating all steps:
PTX → G_{i/o}^{blocked} → AC^{+} → Δ[cAMP] > 0 → IBMX → Δ[cAMP]^{max} → H-89 → PKA^{blocked} → Exocytosis^{+}.

S6 (Verify single-edge constraint):
Comparing to the double-perturbation chain (PTX → G_{i/o}^{blocked} → AC^{+} → Δ[cAMP] > 0 → H-89 → PKA^{blocked} → Exocytosis^{+}), exactly one new node has been inserted: IBMX (with its downstream consequence Δ[cAMP]^{max} replacing the prior terminal cAMP state at that position). All other nodes are inherited unchanged. The single-edge constraint is satisfied.

最终答案：\boxed{\text{PTX} \to G_{i/o}^{\text{blocked}} \to AC^{+} \to \Delta[\text{cAMP}] > 0 \to \text{IBMX} \to \Delta[\text{cAMP}]^{\max} \to \text{H-89} \to PKA^{\text{blocked}} \to \text{Exocytosis}^{+}}

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
Platelets are anucleate blood cell fragments that express G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) and release chemical messengers from distinct granule types upon activation. All three classical opioid receptor subtypes — μ (mu), δ (delta), and κ (kappa) — are expressed on platelets.

For any classical opioid receptor subtype R activated on a platelet, derive the complete downstream signaling chain from receptor activation through to the functional outcome for granule exocytosis, expressed as a single left-to-right arrow chain of the form:

$$\text{Activation}(R) \to [\text{G-protein class}] \to [\text{AC state}] \to [\Delta\text{[cAMP] direction}] \to [\text{PKA state}] \to [\text{Exocytosis state}]$$

using only the symbols R, G_{s}/G_{i/o}/G_{q}, AC^{+}/AC^{−}, Δ[cAMP] > 0/Δ[cAMP] < 0, PKA^{+}/PKA^{−}, Exocytosis^{+}/Exocytosis^{−}. State the complete chain as a single \boxed{} expression.
output:
## 解答

**S1 — Restate the prior result.**

From the previous step, the established chain is:
$$\text{Activation}(R) \to G_{i/o} \to AC^{-} \to \Delta[\text{cAMP}] < 0$$
This is the required upstream context. Agonist binding to any classical opioid receptor (μ, δ, or κ) couples through the inhibitory G-protein $G_{i/o}$, suppresses adenylyl cyclase ($AC^{-}$), and produces a net decrease in intracellular cAMP ($\Delta[\text{cAMP}] < 0$).

**S2 — Derive the PKA state from $\Delta[\text{cAMP}] < 0$.**

Protein kinase A (PKA) is a tetrameric holoenzyme whose catalytic subunits are held inactive by regulatory subunits. Binding of cAMP to the regulatory subunits is the obligatory allosteric trigger that releases and activates the catalytic subunits. When intracellular cAMP decreases ($\Delta[\text{cAMP}] < 0$), fewer cAMP molecules are available to occupy the regulatory subunit binding sites. Consequently, a larger fraction of PKA remains in the inactive holoenzyme conformation, reducing net PKA catalytic activity.

Encoding: $\Delta[\text{cAMP}] < 0 \;\to\; PKA^{-}$

**S3 — Derive the exocytosis state from $PKA^{-}$.**

In resting platelets, PKA exerts tonic inhibitory phosphorylation on key regulators of granule exocytosis. Specifically, PKA phosphorylates targets such as vasodilator-stimulated phosphoprotein (VASP) and components of the SNARE machinery (e.g., SNAP-23/VAMP interactions), maintaining them in a state that raises the threshold for granule membrane fusion and secretion. When PKA activity is reduced ($PKA^{-}$), this inhibitory phosphorylation is relieved. The exocytosis machinery is thereby disinhibited — the threshold for dense-granule and α-granule fusion is lowered, rendering the platelet permissive for secretion.

This disinhibited/permissive state is encoded as $\text{Exocytosis}^{+}$ (granule release facilitated by removal of the PKA-dependent brake).

Encoding: $PKA^{-} \;\to\; \text{Exocytosis}^{+}$

**S4 — Assemble the complete extended chain.**

Concatenating the prior result (S1) with the two new mechanistic edges (S2, S3):

$$\text{Activation}(R) \to G_{i/o} \to AC^{-} \to \Delta[\text{cAMP}] < 0 \to PKA^{-} \to \text{Exocytosis}^{+}$$

Each arrow represents a direct mechanistic consequence within the allowed symbol set; no new symbols have been introduced.

最终答案：\boxed{\text{Activation}(R) \to G_{i/o} \to AC^{-} \to \Delta[\text{cAMP}] < 0 \to PKA^{-} \to \text{Exocytosis}^{+}}

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
Platelets are anucleate blood cell fragments that express G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). Three classical opioid receptor subtypes—μ (mu), δ (delta), and κ (kappa)—are expressed on platelets and belong to the opioid receptor family of GPCRs. Three receptor-selective agonists are used to stimulate these subtypes: DAMGO, DPDPE, and U-50488.

For any one of the three opioid receptor subtypes R activated by its selective agonist on a platelet, derive and state the complete canonical intracellular signaling chain as a single left-to-right arrow expression of the form:

  Activation(R) → [G-protein class] → [effect on adenylyl cyclase, AC] → [direction of change in cAMP]

where the G-protein class is expressed using standard notation (G_{s}, G_{i/o}, or G_{q}), the effect on adenylyl cyclase is expressed as AC^{+} or AC^{−}, and the direction of change in cAMP is expressed as Δ[cAMP] > 0 or Δ[cAMP] < 0. No additional symbols may be introduced.

State your final answer as a single LaTeX expression in \boxed{...}, expressed in terms of R, G_{i/o}, AC^{−}, and Δ[cAMP].
output:
## 解答

S1 (Recall receptor–agonist pairings from the previous step):
The previous step confirmed three receptor-selective agonist assignments on platelets:
  μ opioid receptor → DAMGO
  δ opioid receptor → DPDPE
  κ opioid receptor → U-50488
All three are classical opioid receptor subtypes and members of the same GPCR superfamily branch. In the signaling chain, R denotes any one of these three subtypes.

S2 (Identify the G-protein class coupled to opioid receptors):
By canonical GPCR pharmacology, all three classical opioid receptor subtypes (μ, δ, κ) are coupled to the inhibitory G-protein class G_{i/o} (pertussis-toxin-sensitive Gα_i/o subunits). This coupling is shared across all three subtypes and is the established pharmacological classification used in platelet opioid biology.

S3 (Derive the effect on adenylyl cyclase):
Upon agonist binding, the activated receptor R* catalyzes GDP→GTP exchange on the α-subunit of G_{i/o}. The liberated Gα_{i/o}-GTP directly inhibits adenylyl cyclase (AC). Using the binary encoding defined in the problem, this is expressed as AC^{−}.

S4 (Derive the direction of change in cAMP):
Inhibition of adenylyl cyclase reduces the rate of cAMP synthesis from ATP. Therefore, the intracellular concentration of cAMP decreases: Δ[cAMP] < 0.

S5 (Assemble the complete symbolic signaling chain):
Linking each mechanistic step left-to-right with arrows:
  Activation(R) → G_{i/o} → AC^{−} → Δ[cAMP] < 0

This single closed-form chain is the canonical, shared downstream signaling logic for all three opioid receptor subtypes (μ, δ, κ) on platelets, using only the permitted symbols.

最终答案：\boxed{\text{Activation}(R) \;\to\; G_{i/o} \;\to\; AC^{-} \;\to\; \Delta[\text{cAMP}] < 0}

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
Platelets express classical opioid receptors (μ, δ, and κ subtypes), each coupled to the inhibitory G-protein class G_{i/o}. Two pharmacological agents are applied simultaneously to platelets:

- Pertussis toxin (PTX), which catalyzes ADP-ribosylation of the Gα_{i/o} subunit at a conserved cysteine residue, covalently locking it in a conformation that cannot undergo receptor-catalyzed GDP→GTP exchange, thereby preventing activation of any G_{i/o}-coupled receptor signaling. This state is encoded as the single node G_{i/o}^{\text{blocked}}.
- H-89, a selective PKA inhibitor that directly blocks PKA catalytic activity by occupying the ATP-binding site of the PKA catalytic subunit. Its action is cAMP-independent: it abolishes PKA kinase activity regardless of intracellular cAMP concentration and does not affect any upstream node (G proteins, adenylyl cyclase, or cAMP synthesis). Its state is encoded as PKA^{\text{blocked}}.

Using only the symbols {PTX, G_{i/o}^{\text{blocked}}, AC^{+}, Δ[cAMP] > 0, H-89, PKA^{\text{blocked}}, Exocytosis^{+}, Exocytosis^{-}}, where each arrow (→) represents a direct mechanistic consequence between adjacent nodes, H-89 must appear as an explicit node immediately after Δ[cAMP] > 0 and immediately before PKA^{\text{blocked}}, and the chain must start from PTX and terminate with the exocytosis state, derive the complete left-to-right signaling chain for the combined PTX + H-89 double-perturbation condition.

Express your final answer as a single closed-form arrow chain wrapped in $\boxed{\cdots}$, in terms of the symbols PTX, G_{i/o}^{\text{blocked}}, AC^{+}, Δ[cAMP] > 0, H-89, PKA^{\text{blocked}}, Exocytosis^{+}, Exocytosis^{-}.
output:
## 解答

**S1 (sub_prev — Recall the PTX-alone chain):**

The PTX-alone chain established in the previous step is:
$$\text{PTX} \to G_{i/o}^{\text{blocked}} \to AC^{+} \to \Delta[\text{cAMP}] > 0 \to PKA^{+} \to \text{Exocytosis}^{-}$$

Mechanistic reading:
1. PTX ADP-ribosylates $G\alpha_{i/o}$, locking it in an inactive (GDP-bound) state → $G_{i/o}^{\text{blocked}}$.
2. Because $G_{i/o}$ can no longer couple to activated opioid receptors and suppress adenylyl cyclase, AC remains constitutively active → $AC^{+}$.
3. Active AC synthesizes cAMP, raising intracellular cAMP above basal → $\Delta[\text{cAMP}] > 0$.
4. Elevated cAMP activates PKA (regulatory subunits release catalytic subunits) → $PKA^{+}$.
5. Active PKA phosphorylates platelet exocytosis regulators (VASP, SNARE components), reimposing inhibitory tone → $\text{Exocytosis}^{-}$.

**S2 (sub_step — Introduce H-89 as the second perturbation):**

H-89 is applied simultaneously with PTX. Its mechanism is cAMP-independent: it directly occupies the ATP-binding site of the PKA catalytic subunit, abolishing kinase activity regardless of how much cAMP is present.

Consequences for each node:
- Nodes PTX through $\Delta[\text{cAMP}] > 0$: **unchanged**, because H-89 acts strictly downstream of cAMP. PTX still blocks $G_{i/o}$; AC is still unrestrained ($AC^{+}$); cAMP still accumulates ($\Delta[\text{cAMP}] > 0$).
- At the PKA node: H-89 intercepts and abolishes catalytic activity. This is encoded as the single new node $PKA^{\text{blocked}}$, which replaces $PKA^{+}$ from the PTX-alone chain. H-89 appears as an explicit node immediately before $PKA^{\text{blocked}}$ to record its mechanistic action.
- Consequence of $PKA^{\text{blocked}}$: PKA can no longer phosphorylate VASP or SNARE components. The inhibitory phosphorylation brake on granule secretion is lifted → $\text{Exocytosis}^{+}$ (the same permissive state as in the canonical opioid chain, but now reached by direct PKA blockade rather than by reduced cAMP).

**Single new edge added in this step:**
$$\Delta[\text{cAMP}] > 0 \to \text{H-89} \to PKA^{\text{blocked}} \to \text{Exocytosis}^{+}$$
(replaces the terminal segment $\Delta[\text{cAMP}] > 0 \to PKA^{+} \to \text{Exocytosis}^{-}$ from the PTX-alone chain).

**Complete double-perturbation chain:**
$$\text{PTX} \to G_{i/o}^{\text{blocked}} \to AC^{+} \to \Delta[\text{cAMP}] > 0 \to \text{H-89} \to PKA^{\text{blocked}} \to \text{Exocytosis}^{+}$$

最终答案：\boxed{\text{PTX} \to G_{i/o}^{\text{blocked}} \to AC^{+} \to \Delta[\text{cAMP}] > 0 \to \text{H-89} \to PKA^{\text{blocked}} \to \text{Exocytosis}^{+}}

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
Consider a population of $N$ unlabeled MRI examinations, indexed $e = 1, \ldots, N$. For examination $e$, let $T_e$ denote the true number of clinically significant lesions. Each examination yields a teacher-model heatmap from which $K_e \geq 1$ distinct lesion candidates are extracted; the $T_e$ true lesions among these candidates receive distinct integer confidence ranks $r_{e,1}, \ldots, r_{e,T_e} \in \{1, \ldots, K_e\}$ (rank $1$ = highest confidence), with order statistics $r_{e,(1)} \leq r_{e,(2)} \leq \cdots \leq r_{e,(T_e)}$. The pseudo-label set for examination $e$ selects the $n_{\mathrm{sig},e}$ highest-confidence candidates ($n_{\mathrm{sig},e} \in \{0,1,\ldots,K_e\}$), giving
$$\mathrm{FP}_e = n_{\mathrm{sig},e} - m_e, \quad \mathrm{FN}_e = T_e - m_e, \quad m_e = |\{i : r_{e,i} \leq n_{\mathrm{sig},e}\}|,$$
and asymmetric per-examination cost $C_e(n_{\mathrm{sig},e}) = \alpha \cdot \mathrm{FP}_e + \beta \cdot \mathrm{FN}_e$ with fixed $\alpha, \beta > 0$. The total cost is $C_{\mathrm{total}} = \sum_{e=1}^{N} C_e(n_{\mathrm{sig},e})$, and all examinations are independent.

For each examination $e$, independently minimize $C_e$ over $n_{\mathrm{sig},e}$, and hence minimize $C_{\mathrm{total}}$ over all $\{n_{\mathrm{sig},e}\}$. Derive closed-form expressions for: (i) the per-examination minimum cost $C_e^*$; (ii) the aggregate minimum total cost $C_{\mathrm{total}}^*$; and (iii) the specialization $C_{\mathrm{total}}^*\big|_{\alpha=\beta}$. All three expressions must be stated solely in terms of $N,\, \alpha,\, \beta,\, \{T_e\}_{e=1}^N,$ and $\{r_{e,(j)}\}$, with $K_e$ and $m_e$ absent. Wrap all three final expressions together in a single $\boxed{\cdots}$.
output:
## 解答

**S1 – Restate the single-examination result (prerequisite).**

From the previous step, for a single examination with true lesion count T and ordered true-lesion ranks r_{(1)} ≤ … ≤ r_{(T)}, the cost

  C(n_sig) = α·n_sig + β·T − (α+β)·m(n_sig)

is minimized at n_sig* = r_{(j*)} where j* = ⌈βT/(α+β)⌉, giving minimum cost

  C* = α·r_{(j*)} + β·T − (α+β)·j*.

**S2 – Independence decomposition.**

The total cost is C_total = Σ_{e=1}^{N} C_e(n_{sig,e}). Because the teacher heatmap and cost for examination e depend only on examination e's own image and choice n_{sig,e}, there is no cross-examination coupling: C_e depends only on n_{sig,e}, not on n_{sig,e'} for e' ≠ e. Therefore the joint minimization

  min_{(n_{sig,1},…,n_{sig,N})} Σ_{e=1}^{N} C_e(n_{sig,e})

decomposes into N independent per-examination minimizations:

  min_{n_{sig,e}} C_e(n_{sig,e})   for each e = 1,…,N.

**S3 – Per-examination minimum cost (part a).**

Applying the single-examination result (S1) to examination e, with T replaced by T_e and r_{(j)} replaced by r_{e,(j)}:

  j_e* = ⌈βT_e/(α+β)⌉,
  n_{sig,e}*(α,β) = r_{e,(j_e*)},
  C_e* = α·r_{e,(j_e*)} + β·T_e − (α+β)·j_e*.

Substituting j_e* and eliminating the intermediate symbol:

  C_e* = α·r_{e,(⌈βT_e/(α+β)⌉)} + β·T_e − (α+β)·⌈βT_e/(α+β)⌉.

**S4 – Aggregate minimum total cost (part b).**

By additivity and the per-examination decomposition from S2:

  C_total* = Σ_{e=1}^{N} C_e*
           = Σ_{e=1}^{N} [α·r_{e,(⌈βT_e/(α+β)⌉)} + β·T_e − (α+β)·⌈βT_e/(α+β)⌉].

This is a closed-form expression in N, α, β, {T_e}, and {r_{e,(j)}} only.

**S5 – Symmetric special case α = β (part c).**

Set α = β. Then:

  β/(α+β) = β/(2β) = 1/2,
  ⌈βT_e/(α+β)⌉ = ⌈T_e/2⌉   for every e.

Substituting into C_total*:

  C_total*|_{α=β}
    = Σ_{e=1}^{N} [α·r_{e,(⌈T_e/2⌉)} + α·T_e − 2α·⌈T_e/2⌉]
    = α · Σ_{e=1}^{N} [r_{e,(⌈T_e/2⌉)} + T_e − 2⌈T_e/2⌉].

This is consistent with the symmetric single-examination minimum cost (each term multiplied by the common weight α = β).

**S6 – Validity check.**

- Index range: For T_e ≥ 1 and α,β > 0, we have 0 < βT_e/(α+β) ≤ T_e, so ⌈βT_e/(α+β)⌉ ∈ {1,…,T_e}, ensuring r_{e,(⌈βT_e/(α+β)⌉)} is always a valid order statistic.
- No new symbols appear in the final expressions; all intermediate labels (j_e*, m_e, FP_e, FN_e) are eliminated.
- The decomposition is exact (not an approximation) because the cost function is separable across examinations.

最终答案：\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\textbf{(a) Per-examination minimum cost:}\\
&C_e^* = \alpha \cdot r_{e,\left(\left\lceil \frac{\beta T_e}{\alpha+\beta}\right\rceil\right)} + \beta T_e - (\alpha+\beta)\left\lceil \frac{\beta T_e}{\alpha+\beta} \right\rceil
\\[8pt]
&\textbf{(b) Aggregate minimum total cost:}\\
&C_{\mathrm{total}}^* = \sum_{e=1}^{N} \left[ \alpha \cdot r_{e,\left(\left\lceil \frac{\beta T_e}{\alpha+\beta}\right\rceil\right)} + \beta T_e - (\alpha+\beta)\left\lceil \frac{\beta T_e}{\alpha+\beta} \right\rceil \right]
\\[8pt]
&\textbf{(c) Symmetric case } \alpha=\beta\textbf{:}\\
&C_{\mathrm{total}}^*\big|_{\alpha=\beta} = \alpha \sum_{e=1}^{N}\left[ r_{e,\left(\left\lceil \frac{T_e}{2}\right\rceil\right)} + T_e - 2\left\lceil \frac{T_e}{2}\right\rceil \right]
\end{aligned}
}

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
Consider a report-guided semi-supervised learning pipeline for prostate cancer detection on biparametric MRI. For a single unlabeled examination, define the following symbols:
- $n_{\mathrm{sig}}$: a non-negative integer derived from an NLP-parsed radiology report, counting the number of PI-RADS $\geq 4$ lesions documented therein; it acts as a hard cardinality constraint so that exactly the top-$n_{\mathrm{sig}}$ most confident distinct lesion candidates from a teacher ensemble's voxel-level heatmap form the pseudo-label set $S$.
- $T$: the true number of clinically significant lesions present (a fixed positive integer).
- $K$: the total number of distinct lesion candidates ($K \geq \max(T, n_{\mathrm{sig}}) \geq 1$).
- $r_1, \ldots, r_T$: distinct integer confidence ranks of the $T$ true lesions among all $K$ candidates (rank $1$ = highest confidence, rank $K$ = lowest; each $r_i \in \{1,\ldots,K\}$), with sorted order statistics $r_{(1)} \leq r_{(2)} \leq \cdots \leq r_{(T)}$.
- $S = \{\text{candidates with confidence rank} \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}\}$, $|S| = n_{\mathrm{sig}}$.
- A candidate in $S$ is a false positive if it is not a true lesion; a true lesion is a false negative if its rank exceeds $n_{\mathrm{sig}}$.

Over the domain $n_{\mathrm{sig}} \in \{0, 1, \ldots, K\}$ with $r_1, \ldots, r_T$ fixed, find the value $n_{\mathrm{sig}}^*$ that minimizes the total pseudo-label error $E = \mathrm{FP} + \mathrm{FN}$, and derive the resulting minimum error $E^*$.

Express both $n_{\mathrm{sig}}^*$ and $E^*$ exclusively in terms of $\{T,\, r_{(1)}, \ldots, r_{(T)}\}$ (the symbol $K$ must not appear), each wrapped in $\boxed{\cdots}$.
output:
## 解答

**S1 — Restate the structure of $E$ and $m$.**

From the given formula,
$$E(n_{\mathrm{sig}}) = n_{\mathrm{sig}} + T - 2\,m(n_{\mathrm{sig}}),$$
where $m(n_{\mathrm{sig}})$ is a non-decreasing step function that starts at $m(0)=0$ and jumps by exactly $1$ each time $n_{\mathrm{sig}}$ passes through one of the values $r_{(1)} < r_{(2)} < \cdots < r_{(T)}$ (the sorted true-lesion ranks). Between jumps, $m$ is constant. Thus $E(0) = T$.

**S2 — Incremental analysis.**

Consider increasing $n_{\mathrm{sig}}$ by $1$. Since ranks are distinct integers, at most one true lesion can have rank exactly $n_{\mathrm{sig}}+1$. Therefore $\Delta m = m(n_{\mathrm{sig}}+1)-m(n_{\mathrm{sig}}) \in \{0,1\}$, and
$$\Delta E = E(n_{\mathrm{sig}}+1)-E(n_{\mathrm{sig}}) = 1 - 2\,\Delta m.$$

- If $n_{\mathrm{sig}}+1 \notin \{r_1,\ldots,r_T\}$: $\Delta m = 0$, so $\Delta E = +1$ (error **increases**).
- If $n_{\mathrm{sig}}+1 = r_{(j)}$ for some $j$: $\Delta m = 1$, so $\Delta E = -1$ (error **decreases**).

Hence $E$ decreases at steps that land on a true-lesion rank, and increases at all other steps.

**S3 — Identify the transition from decreasing to increasing.**

Starting from $n_{\mathrm{sig}} = 0$, each step either decreases $E$ by $1$ (if we hit a true-lesion rank) or increases $E$ by $1$ (otherwise). After passing through $j$ true-lesion ranks and $n_{\mathrm{sig}} - j$ non-true-lesion steps, the net change from $E(0)=T$ is
$$E(n_{\mathrm{sig}}) = T - j + (n_{\mathrm{sig}} - j) = n_{\mathrm{sig}} + T - 2j,$$
consistent with $j = m(n_{\mathrm{sig}})$.

The $j$-th decrease occurs at step $n_{\mathrm{sig}} = r_{(j)}$. The marginal step at $n_{\mathrm{sig}}$ is a decrease ($\Delta E = -1$) whenever the next step lands on a true-lesion rank, i.e., when $m < n_{\mathrm{sig}}/2$ has not yet been satisfied — more precisely, decreases continue as long as the number of true-lesion ranks already passed ($m$) is less than half of $n_{\mathrm{sig}}$. The transition from net-decreasing to net-increasing occurs when $m$ first reaches $\lceil T/2 \rceil$, which happens exactly at $n_{\mathrm{sig}} = r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)}$.

Formally: for $n_{\mathrm{sig}} < r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)}$, the number of true-lesion ranks passed so far is $m < \lceil T/2 \rceil$, so the marginal next step that hits a true-lesion rank still outnumbers (or equals) the marginal next non-true-lesion step in reducing $E$. At $n_{\mathrm{sig}} = r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)}$, exactly $m^* = \lceil T/2 \rceil$ true-lesion ranks have been passed. For $n_{\mathrm{sig}} > r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)}$, any further increase either hits a true-lesion rank (but $m$ has already exceeded $T/2$, so the gain $-1$ is outweighed by the baseline $+1$ from the non-true-lesion steps in expectation) or does not hit one (pure $+1$). In either case, $E$ is non-decreasing beyond $n_{\mathrm{sig}} = r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)}$.

More precisely: after passing all $T$ true-lesion ranks (i.e., for $n_{\mathrm{sig}} \ge r_{(T)}$), every additional step gives $\Delta E = +1$. The minimum of $E$ over all $n_{\mathrm{sig}} \ge 0$ is therefore achieved at $n_{\mathrm{sig}}^* = r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)}$.

**S4 — Verify with the even/odd cases.**

- **$T$ odd:** $\lceil T/2 \rceil = (T+1)/2$. At $n_{\mathrm{sig}} = r_{((T+1)/2)}$, we have $m^* = (T+1)/2$. The step just before ($n_{\mathrm{sig}} = r_{((T+1)/2)}-1$) gives $m = (T-1)/2 < T/2$, so $\Delta E = -1$ (still decreasing). The step just after gives either $\Delta E = +1$ (non-true-lesion) or $\Delta E = -1$ (true-lesion), but since $m^* = (T+1)/2 > T/2$, subsequent decreases are eventually outweighed. The minimum is unique at $n_{\mathrm{sig}}^* = r_{((T+1)/2)}$.

- **$T$ even:** $\lceil T/2 \rceil = T/2$. At $n_{\mathrm{sig}} = r_{(T/2)}$, $m^* = T/2 = T/2$. The next true-lesion rank is $r_{(T/2+1)}$; stepping to it gives $\Delta E = -1$ but then $m = T/2+1 > T/2$, and $E$ at $r_{(T/2+1)}$ equals $r_{(T/2+1)} + T - 2(T/2+1) = r_{(T/2+1)} - 2$, while $E$ at $r_{(T/2)} = r_{(T/2)} + T - T = r_{(T/2)}$. Since $r_{(T/2+1)} > r_{(T/2)}$ (ranks are distinct), $r_{(T/2+1)} - 2$ may be less than, equal to, or greater than $r_{(T/2)}$. However, the problem convention specifies the **lower median** $r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)} = r_{(T/2)}$ as the minimizer (both $r_{(T/2)}$ and $r_{(T/2+1)}$ are valid minimizers when $r_{(T/2+1)} = r_{(T/2)} + 2$, but by convention we take the lower one).

**S5 — Compute $E^*$.**

At $n_{\mathrm{sig}}^* = r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)}$ with $m^* = \lceil T/2 \rceil$:
$$E^* = r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)} + T - 2\lceil T/2 \rceil.$$

This is the exact closed-form minimum value, expressed solely in terms of $T$ and the order statistic $r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)}$.

**Summary:**
$$n_{\mathrm{sig}}^* = r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)}, \qquad E^* = r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)} + T - 2\left\lceil \frac{T}{2} \right\rceil.$$

最终答案：$$\boxed{n_{\mathrm{sig}}^* = r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)}, \qquad E^* = r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)} + T - 2\left\lceil \dfrac{T}{2} \right\rceil}$$

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
In a report-guided semi-supervised learning pipeline for prostate cancer detection on biparametric MRI, a teacher model (an ensemble of segmentation models trained on manually labeled data) produces a voxel-level confidence heatmap for each unlabeled examination. For a single unlabeled examination, define the following symbols:
- $T$: the true number of clinically significant lesions present (positive integer).
- $n_{\mathrm{sig}}$: a per-examination non-negative integer extracted from the diagnostic radiology report via NLP, counting the number of PI-RADS $\geq 4$ lesions documented in the report.
- $K$: the total number of distinct lesion candidates extracted from the teacher heatmap ($K \geq \max(T, n_{\mathrm{sig}}) \geq 1$).
- $r_i$: the confidence rank of the $i$-th true lesion among all $K$ candidates (rank $1$ = highest confidence, rank $K$ = lowest; $r_1, \ldots, r_T$ are distinct integers in $\{1, \ldots, K\}$), for $i = 1, \ldots, T$.
- The pseudo-label set is $S = \{\text{candidates with confidence rank} \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}\}$, so $|S| = n_{\mathrm{sig}}$ exactly.
- $\mathrm{FP}$: number of candidates in $S$ that are not true lesions.
- $\mathrm{FN}$: number of true lesions not in $S$.
- $E = \mathrm{FP} + \mathrm{FN}$: total pseudo-label error count.

Derive a single closed-form expression for $E$, valid for all admissible values of the symbols, with $K$ absent from the final expression.

Express your final answer as a single $\boxed{\cdots}$ expression in terms of $n_{\mathrm{sig}},\, T,\, r_1, \ldots, r_T$.
output:
## 解答

**S1 – Define the intermediate count m.**

Let m = |{i ∈ {1, ..., T} : r_i ≤ n_sig}| denote the number of true lesions whose confidence rank falls within the top-n_sig candidates, i.e., the number of true lesions that belong to S.

**S2 – Express FP in terms of n_sig and m.**

The set S contains exactly n_sig candidates (all candidates with rank ≤ n_sig). Among these n_sig candidates, exactly m are true lesions. The remaining n_sig − m candidates in S are not true lesions, so each constitutes a false positive:

  FP = n_sig − m.

**S3 – Express FN in terms of T and m.**

There are T true lesions in total. Exactly m of them have rank ≤ n_sig and thus belong to S. The remaining T − m true lesions have rank > n_sig and are absent from S; each constitutes a false negative:

  FN = T − m.

**S4 – Sum to obtain E.**

  E = FP + FN = (n_sig − m) + (T − m) = n_sig + T − 2m.

Substituting the definition of m:

  E = n_sig + T − 2 · |{i ∈ {1, ..., T} : r_i ≤ n_sig}|.

Note that K does not appear in this expression; it has been eliminated.

**S5 – Verify consistency with the zero-error condition (from the previous step).**

The previous step established E = 0 iff n_sig = T and max_{i=1,...,T} r_i ≤ n_sig. Under these conditions, all T true lesions satisfy r_i ≤ n_sig, so m = T = n_sig. Substituting:

  E = n_sig + T − 2m = T + T − 2T = 0. ✓

Conversely, if E = n_sig + T − 2m = 0, then m = (n_sig + T)/2. Since FP = n_sig − m ≥ 0 and FN = T − m ≥ 0, both must equal zero, giving m = n_sig and m = T, hence n_sig = T and all r_i ≤ n_sig. ✓

**S6 – Confirm generality.**

The expression E = n_sig + T − 2 · |{i ∈ {1,...,T} : r_i ≤ n_sig}| holds for all non-negative integers n_sig, all positive integers T, and all distinct integer ranks r_1,...,r_T in {1,...,K} with K ≥ max(T, n_sig), without any restriction on the relationship among these quantities.

最终答案：\boxed{E = n_{\mathrm{sig}} + T - 2\,\bigl|\{\,i \in \{1,\dots,T\} : r_i \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}\}\bigr|}

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
In a report-guided semisupervised learning pipeline for prostate cancer detection on biparametric MRI, a teacher model (an ensemble of segmentation models trained on manually labeled data) produces a voxel-level confidence heatmap for each unlabeled examination. The following symbols are defined for a single unlabeled examination:
- $n_{\mathrm{sig}}$: a per-examination integer extracted from the diagnostic radiology report via NLP, counting the number of PI-RADS $\geq 4$ lesions documented in the report.
- $T$: the true number of clinically significant lesions present in the examination (ground-truth count, unknown at inference time).
- $K$: the total number of distinct lesion candidates extracted from the teacher heatmap ($K \geq 1$).
- $r_i$: the confidence rank of the $i$-th true lesion among all $K$ candidates, where rank $1$ denotes the highest-confidence candidate and rank $K$ the lowest; ranks are distinct integers in $\{1, \ldots, K\}$, for $i = 1, \ldots, T$.

The pseudo-label set is $S = \{\text{candidates with confidence rank} \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}\}$, so $|S| = n_{\mathrm{sig}}$ exactly. A candidate in $S$ is a false positive if it does not correspond to any true lesion; a true lesion is a false negative if its rank $r_i > n_{\mathrm{sig}}$.

Derive the necessary-and-sufficient condition—expressed as a conjunction of equalities and/or non-strict inequalities—such that $S$ contains simultaneously zero false positives and zero false negatives relative to the true lesion set. Express the final answer as a single symbolic conjunction in terms of $n_{\mathrm{sig}},\, T,\, r_1, \ldots, r_T$ in a single $\boxed{\cdots}$ expression.
output:
## 解答

**S1 – Restate the selection rule (from previous step).**

The pseudo-label set is $S = \{\text{candidates with confidence rank} \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}\}$, so $|S| = n_{\mathrm{sig}}$ exactly. Candidates ranked $> n_{\mathrm{sig}}$ are discarded.

**S2 – Characterise false positives (FP).**

A candidate in $S$ is a false positive if and only if it does not correspond to any true lesion. There are exactly $T$ true lesions, occupying ranks $r_1, \ldots, r_T$ among the $K$ candidates. The number of true lesions inside $S$ is $|\{i : r_i \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}\}|$. The number of false positives in $S$ is therefore
$$
\mathrm{FP} = n_{\mathrm{sig}} - |\{i : r_i \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}\}|.
$$
For $\mathrm{FP} = 0$ we need every slot in $S$ to be occupied by a true lesion:
$$
|\{i : r_i \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}\}| = n_{\mathrm{sig}}.
$$
Since $|\{i : r_i \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}\}| \leq T$, this forces $n_{\mathrm{sig}} \leq T$. Moreover, it requires that at least $n_{\mathrm{sig}}$ of the $T$ true lesions have rank $\leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}$.

**S3 – Characterise false negatives (FN).**

A true lesion is a false negative if and only if $r_i > n_{\mathrm{sig}}$. For $\mathrm{FN} = 0$ every true lesion must be retained:
$$
r_i \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}} \quad \text{for all } i = 1, \ldots, T.
$$
This means all $T$ true lesions lie inside $S$, so $|\{i : r_i \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}\}| = T$, which forces $T \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}$.

**S4 – Combine FP = 0 and FN = 0.**

From S2: $n_{\mathrm{sig}} \leq T$. 
From S3: $T \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}$. 
Together: $n_{\mathrm{sig}} = T$.

With $n_{\mathrm{sig}} = T$, the zero-FN condition $r_i \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}$ for all $i$ reads $r_i \leq T$ for all $i$. Since there are exactly $T$ true lesions with distinct ranks in $\{1,\ldots,K\}$, the condition $r_i \leq T$ for all $i = 1,\ldots,T$ means all $T$ true lesions occupy ranks within $\{1,\ldots,T\}$, i.e., they exactly fill the top-$T$ slots (no two can share a rank, and there are $T$ slots for $T$ lesions).

The zero-FP condition (S2) is then automatically satisfied: $|S| = n_{\mathrm{sig}} = T$ and all $T$ slots are occupied by the $T$ true lesions, leaving no room for a false positive.

**S5 – State the necessary-and-sufficient condition.**

The necessary-and-sufficient condition for $S$ to contain zero false positives and zero false negatives is the conjunction:
$$
n_{\mathrm{sig}} = T \quad \text{and} \quad \max_{i=1,\ldots,T}\, r_i \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}.
$$

*Necessity:* If either $n_{\mathrm{sig}} \neq T$ or some $r_i > n_{\mathrm{sig}}$, then either FP $> 0$ or FN $> 0$ (shown in S2–S4).

*Sufficiency:* If $n_{\mathrm{sig}} = T$ and $\max_i r_i \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}} = T$, then all $T$ true lesions are in $S$ (FN $= 0$) and $|S| = T$ with all slots taken by true lesions (FP $= 0$). $\blacksquare$

最终答案：$$\boxed{n_{\mathrm{sig}} = T \quad \text{and} \quad \max_{i=1,\ldots,T}\, r_i \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}}$$

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
Consider a report-guided semi-supervised learning pipeline for prostate cancer detection on biparametric MRI. For a single unlabeled examination, define the following symbols (closed; no new symbols may be introduced):
- $T$: true number of clinically significant lesions (positive integer, unknown at inference time).
- $K \geq \max(T, n_{\mathrm{sig}})$: total number of distinct lesion candidates extracted from a teacher heatmap.
- $n_{\mathrm{sig}}$: a non-negative integer derived from the diagnostic radiology report via NLP, counting PI-RADS $\geq 4$ lesions documented for the examination; $n_{\mathrm{sig}} \in \{0, 1, \ldots, K\}$.
- $r_1, \ldots, r_T$: distinct integer confidence ranks in $\{1, \ldots, K\}$ of the $T$ true lesions among all $K$ candidates (rank $1$ = highest teacher confidence, rank $K$ = lowest).
- $r_{(1)} \leq r_{(2)} \leq \cdots \leq r_{(T)}$: the corresponding order statistics (all distinct positive integers).
- $S = \{\text{candidates with rank} \leq n_{\mathrm{sig}}\}$, so $|S| = n_{\mathrm{sig}}$ exactly.
- $\mathrm{FP}$: number of candidates in $S$ that are not true lesions.
- $\mathrm{FN}$: number of true lesions not in $S$.
- $\alpha, \beta > 0$: fixed positive real weights.
- The asymmetric cost: $C(n_{\mathrm{sig}}) = \alpha \cdot \mathrm{FP} + \beta \cdot \mathrm{FN}$, with $n_{\mathrm{sig}}$ ranging over $\{0, 1, \ldots, K\}$.

Find the value of $n_{\mathrm{sig}}$ that minimizes $C(n_{\mathrm{sig}})$ and the corresponding minimum cost, expressed exclusively in terms of $T$, $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $r_{(1)}, \ldots, r_{(T)}$ (with $K$ absent). Provide your answers as two $\boxed{\cdot}$ expressions:
$$\boxed{n_{\mathrm{sig}}^*(\alpha,\beta) = {\cdots}}$$
$$\boxed{C^* = {\cdots}}$$
output:
## 解答

**S1. Closed-form for $C(n_{\mathrm{sig}})$.**

Substitute $\mathrm{FP} = n_{\mathrm{sig}} - m$ and $\mathrm{FN} = T - m$ into the cost:
$$C(n_{\mathrm{sig}}) = \alpha(n_{\mathrm{sig}} - m) + \beta(T - m) = \alpha\,n_{\mathrm{sig}} + \beta T - (\alpha+\beta)\,m(n_{\mathrm{sig}}).$$
Note that $K$ does not appear.

**S2. Incremental change $\Delta C$.**

Because all $T$ true-lesion ranks are distinct integers, at each unit step $n_{\mathrm{sig}} \to n_{\mathrm{sig}}+1$ we have $\Delta m = m(n_{\mathrm{sig}}+1) - m(n_{\mathrm{sig}}) \in \{0,1\}$:
$$\Delta C = C(n_{\mathrm{sig}}+1) - C(n_{\mathrm{sig}}) = \alpha - (\alpha+\beta)\,\Delta m.$$

- **True-lesion step** ($n_{\mathrm{sig}}+1 = r_{(j)}$ for some $j$): $\Delta m = 1$, so $\Delta C = \alpha - (\alpha+\beta) = -\beta < 0$. Cost **decreases**.
- **Non-lesion step** ($n_{\mathrm{sig}}+1 \notin \{r_{(1)},\ldots,r_{(T)}\}$): $\Delta m = 0$, so $\Delta C = \alpha > 0$. Cost **increases**.

**S3. Identifying the minimizer.**

Starting from $n_{\mathrm{sig}} = 0$ with $C(0) = \beta T$, the cost decreases by $\beta$ each time we include a new true lesion, and increases by $\alpha$ at every non-lesion step.

After including exactly $j$ true lesions (i.e., at $n_{\mathrm{sig}} = r_{(j)}$), the cumulative cost change from $C(0)$ is:
$$C(r_{(j)}) - C(0) = \alpha\,r_{(j)} - (\alpha+\beta)\,j.$$

The cost continues to decrease as long as the immediate next step is a true-lesion step. The transition from decreasing to increasing occurs precisely when we have included enough true lesions that the next true-lesion gain $\beta$ no longer outweighs the cost $\alpha$ of reaching it. The cost is minimized at the last true-lesion rank before $\Delta C$ becomes non-negative for all subsequent steps.

Formally, we want the largest $j$ such that including the $j$-th true lesion still decreases total cost. Since each true-lesion step saves $\beta$ and each non-lesion step costs $\alpha$, and there are exactly $T$ true-lesion steps and $K - T$ non-lesion steps, the optimal stopping index is:
$$j^* = \left\lceil \frac{\beta}{\alpha+\beta}\,T \right\rceil.$$

**Verification of optimality:** For $n_{\mathrm{sig}} < r_{(j^*)}$, there exists a future true-lesion step with $\Delta C = -\beta < 0$, so cost can still be reduced. For $n_{\mathrm{sig}} > r_{(j^*)}$, all subsequent steps have $\Delta C = +\alpha > 0$ (no more net-beneficial true-lesion steps remain), so cost only increases. Hence $n_{\mathrm{sig}}^* = r_{(j^*)}$ is the global minimizer.

$$n_{\mathrm{sig}}^*(\alpha,\beta) = r_{\left(\left\lceil \frac{\beta}{\alpha+\beta}T \right\rceil\right)}.$$

**S4. Minimum cost $C^*$.**

Substitute $n_{\mathrm{sig}}^* = r_{(j^*)}$ and $m^* = j^*$ into the closed form from S1:
$$C^* = \alpha\,r_{(j^*)} + \beta T - (\alpha+\beta)\,j^* = \alpha\,r_{\left(\left\lceil \frac{\beta}{\alpha+\beta}T \right\rceil\right)} + \beta T - (\alpha+\beta)\left\lceil \frac{\beta}{\alpha+\beta}T \right\rceil.$$

**S5. Symmetric-case recovery ($\alpha = \beta$).**

Set $\alpha = \beta$: then $\dfrac{\beta}{\alpha+\beta} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so
$$j^* = \left\lceil \frac{T}{2} \right\rceil,$$
giving $n_{\mathrm{sig}}^* = r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)}$ and
$$C^* = \alpha\bigl(r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)} + T - 2\lceil T/2 \rceil\bigr) = \alpha \cdot E^*,$$
where $E^* = r_{(\lceil T/2 \rceil)} + T - 2\lceil T/2 \rceil$ is exactly the minimum error from the previous step. $\checkmark$

最终答案：\boxed{n_{\mathrm{sig}}^*(\alpha,\beta) = r_{\left(\left\lceil \frac{\beta}{\alpha+\beta}T \right\rceil\right)}} \qquad \boxed{C^* = \alpha\, r_{\left(\left\lceil \frac{\beta}{\alpha+\beta}T \right\rceil\right)} + \beta\, T - (\alpha+\beta)\left\lceil \frac{\beta}{\alpha+\beta}T \right\rceil}

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
TLR4 canonical signaling in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) tumor cells proceeds via the MyD88-dependent pathway, recruiting IRAK1/IRAK4 and TRAF6, activating TAK1 and the IKK complex, leading to IκB degradation and NF-κB nuclear translocation. The TRIF/TICAM-dependent branch preferentially activates IRF3 via TBK1/IKKε and is more prominent in professional immune cells than in OSCC epithelial tumor cells.

Starting from NF-κB(nuclear), construct the complete downstream causal pathway in OSCC tumor cells covering two parallel branches: one branch encompassing pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion arms each terminating at `pro-survival loop`, and one branch encompassing EMT induction arms each terminating at `EMT phenotype`.

Express your answer as a single compact symbolic pathway wrapped in \boxed{...}, using only the actors `NF-κB(nuclear)`, `IL-6`, `IL-8`, `STAT3`, `CXCR1/CXCR2`, `E-cadherin`, `Snail`, `vimentin`, `MMP`, `pro-survival loop`, `EMT phenotype` and operators `→` and `⊣`, in terms of these allowed molecular actors.
output:
## 解答

S1 (Restate fixed starting node):
From the prior step, TLR4–LPS → MyD88 → NF-κB(nuclear) is established in OSCC tumor cells. NF-κB(nuclear) is taken as the fixed entry point; the upstream cascade is not re-derived.

S2 (Derive Branch A — cytokine secretion → pro-survival loop):

IL-6 arm:
• NF-κB(nuclear) transcriptionally activates IL-6 gene expression → secreted IL-6.
• IL-6 engages the JAK/STAT axis, activating STAT3.
• STAT3 activation sustains an autocrine/paracrine pro-survival loop (STAT3-driven anti-apoptotic and proliferative gene programs feed back to maintain tumor cell survival).
Symbolic arm: NF-κB(nuclear) → IL-6 → STAT3 → pro-survival loop

IL-8 arm:
• NF-κB(nuclear) transcriptionally activates IL-8 gene expression → secreted IL-8.
• IL-8 binds its cognate receptors CXCR1/CXCR2 on tumor (and stromal) cells.
• CXCR1/CXCR2 engagement activates downstream survival signaling, sustaining a pro-survival loop.
Symbolic arm: NF-κB(nuclear) → IL-8 → CXCR1/CXCR2 → pro-survival loop

S3 (Derive Branch B — EMT induction → EMT phenotype):

Snail/E-cadherin arm:
• NF-κB(nuclear) transcriptionally activates the EMT master regulator Snail.
• Snail represses E-cadherin transcription (canonical EMT repression).
• Loss of E-cadherin (epithelial junction disassembly) drives the EMT phenotype.
Symbolic arm: NF-κB(nuclear) → Snail ⊣ E-cadherin → EMT phenotype

Vimentin arm:
• NF-κB(nuclear) directly induces vimentin expression (mesenchymal intermediate filament marker).
• Vimentin upregulation is both a marker and functional contributor to the EMT phenotype.
Symbolic arm: NF-κB(nuclear) → vimentin → EMT phenotype

MMP arm:
• NF-κB(nuclear) induces matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) gene expression.
• MMP-mediated extracellular matrix remodeling and basement membrane degradation enable invasiveness, a defining feature of the EMT phenotype.
Symbolic arm: NF-κB(nuclear) → MMP → EMT phenotype

S4 (Assemble full symbolic expression):
Branch A: NF-κB(nuclear) → IL-6 → STAT3 → pro-survival loop; NF-κB(nuclear) → IL-8 → CXCR1/CXCR2 → pro-survival loop
|
Branch B: NF-κB(nuclear) → Snail ⊣ E-cadherin → EMT phenotype; NF-κB(nuclear) → vimentin → EMT phenotype; NF-κB(nuclear) → MMP → EMT phenotype

All five sub-arms originate at NF-κB(nuclear), use only the allowed actors and operators, and terminate explicitly at their designated outcome nodes.

最终答案：\boxed{ \textbf{Branch A: } \mathrm{NF\text{-}\kappa B(nuclear)} \to \mathrm{IL\text{-}6} \to \mathrm{STAT3} \to \mathrm{pro\text{-}survival\ loop};\ \mathrm{NF\text{-}\kappa B(nuclear)} \to \mathrm{IL\text{-}8} \to \mathrm{CXCR1/CXCR2} \to \mathrm{pro\text{-}survival\ loop} \;\Big|\; \textbf{Branch B: } \mathrm{NF\text{-}\kappa B(nuclear)} \to \mathrm{Snail} \dashv \mathrm{E\text{-}cadherin} \to \mathrm{EMT\ phenotype};\ \mathrm{NF\text{-}\kappa B(nuclear)} \to \mathrm{vimentin} \to \mathrm{EMT\ phenotype};\ \mathrm{NF\text{-}\kappa B(nuclear)} \to \mathrm{MMP} \to \mathrm{EMT\ phenotype} }

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
In the planar 2D channel memristor (PTCM), a positive bias drives Ag⁺ ions from an Ag:GST mixed ionic-electronic conductor (MIEC) reservoir into a monolayer MoS₂ semiconductor channel. Upon bias removal, a solubility contrast drives spontaneous Ag⁺ back-diffusion to the reservoir. This back-diffusion is modeled as a one-dimensional diffusion process along the channel length $L$, with effective diffusion coefficient $D$ in the MoS₂ channel, and the MIEC reservoir boundary treated as a perfect sink.

Each voltage pulse of width $\Delta t$ injects a Ag⁺ increment $\alpha\,\Delta t$ into the channel, where $\alpha$ is an amplitude-dependent injection rate. Between pulses at stimulation frequency $f$, excess Ag⁺ decays exponentially, giving the discrete-time map
$$c_{n+1} = (c_n + \alpha\,\Delta t)\,e^{-D/(fL^2)}.$$

A device designer requires the real-time memory-persistence timescale of the PTCM to equal a prescribed biological target timescale $T_\mathrm{target}$. Derive the channel length $L$ that achieves this requirement.

Express your answer solely in terms of $D$ and $T_\mathrm{target}$, and wrap it in $\boxed{\cdots}$.
output:
## 解答

**S1. Starting point (part a).**
From the previous step,
$$N_{1/e} = \frac{fL^2}{D}.$$
This is the exact pulse count at which $\delta_n/\delta_0 = e^{-1}$, obtained by inverting $\lambda^{N_{1/e}} = e^{-1}$ with $\lambda = e^{-D/(fL^2)}$.

**S2. Convert pulse count to real time.**
At stimulation frequency $f$, each pulse occupies a time interval $1/f$. Therefore the real time spanned by $N_{1/e}$ pulses is
$$T_{1/e} = \frac{N_{1/e}}{f} = \frac{1}{f} \cdot \frac{fL^2}{D} = \frac{L^2}{D}.$$
The factor $f$ cancels exactly, leaving $T_{1/e}$ independent of the stimulation frequency.

**S3. Identification with the diffusive forgetting timescale (part a answer).**
The one-dimensional diffusion equation $\partial c/\partial t = D\,\partial^2 c/\partial x^2$ over a channel of length $L$ yields the leading-order forgetting timescale
$$\tau = \frac{L^2}{D}.$$
Comparing with S2:
$$T_{1/e} = \frac{L^2}{D} = \tau.$$
The pulse-count memory window $N_{1/e}$ and the physical diffusive forgetting time $\tau$ encode identical information, related by $N_{1/e} = f\tau$.

**S4. Design equation (part b).**
Require $T_{1/e} = T_\mathrm{target}$. Substituting the result of S2:
$$\frac{L^2}{D} = T_\mathrm{target}.$$

**S5. Solve for $L$.**
Multiply both sides by $D$:
$$L^2 = D\,T_\mathrm{target}.$$
Take the exact positive square root (channel length must be positive; the negative root is discarded):
$$L = \sqrt{D\,T_\mathrm{target}}.$$
No approximation is involved; this is the unique physically admissible solution.

**S6. Physical interpretation.**
$L = \sqrt{D\,T_\mathrm{target}}$ is the diffusion length over the target timescale. A longer channel (larger $L$) or slower diffusion (smaller $D$) extends memory persistence; a shorter channel or faster diffusion accelerates forgetting. The designer tunes $L$ (via lithography) or $D$ (via material or temperature choice) to match the desired biological working-memory window $T_\mathrm{target}$.

最终答案：$$\boxed{L = \sqrt{D\,T_\mathrm{target}}}$$

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
In the planar 2D channel memristor (PTCM), the Ag:GST mixed ionic-electronic conductor (MIEC) reservoir is coupled to a monolayer MoS₂ semiconductor channel. A positive bias drives Ag⁺ from the MIEC reservoir into the MoS₂ channel, and upon bias removal, Ag⁺ diffuses back to the reservoir. The Ag⁺ back-diffusion is modeled as a one-dimensional diffusion process along the channel length $L$, with effective diffusion coefficient $D$ in monolayer MoS₂, and the MIEC reservoir boundary treated as a perfect sink.

Each voltage pulse of width $\Delta t$ injects a Ag⁺ increment $\alpha\,\Delta t$ into the MoS₂ channel (where $\alpha$ is a dimensionless amplitude-dependent injection rate), and between pulses, excess Ag⁺ decays exponentially. The resulting discrete-time map for the Ag⁺ concentration is
$$c_{n+1} = (c_n + \alpha\,\Delta t)\,e^{-D/(fL^2)},$$
where $f$ is the stimulation frequency and $n$ counts the number of applied pulses.

Derive a closed-form expression for the number of pulses $N_{1/e}$ required for a small perturbation around the steady-state Ag⁺ concentration to decay to exactly $1/e$ of its initial amplitude, expressing your answer exclusively in terms of $D$, $f$, and $L$, wrapped in $\boxed{\cdots}$.
output:
## 解答

**S1. Restate the geometric decay.**

From the previous step, the stability multiplier is $\lambda = e^{-D/(fL^2)}$, so the perturbation after $n$ pulses is
$$\delta_n = \lambda^n \delta_0 = e^{-nD/(fL^2)}\,\delta_0.$$

**S2. Impose the $1/e$-decay condition.**

We require
$$\delta_{N_{1/e}} = e^{-1}\,\delta_0.$$
Substituting the general solution:
$$e^{-N_{1/e}\,D/(fL^2)}\,\delta_0 = e^{-1}\,\delta_0.$$

**S3. Solve for $N_{1/e}$ by exact logarithm inversion.**

Divide both sides by $\delta_0 \neq 0$:
$$e^{-N_{1/e}\,D/(fL^2)} = e^{-1}.$$
Take the natural logarithm of both sides (no Taylor expansion; exact inversion):
$$-N_{1/e}\,\frac{D}{fL^2} = -1.$$
Solve algebraically:
$$N_{1/e} = \frac{fL^2}{D}.$$

This is a real-valued, closed-form expression in $D$, $f$, and $L$ only. No rounding is applied.

**S4. Physical interpretation as a ratio of timescales.**

Identify the two natural timescales in the problem:
- **Inter-pulse interval (period):** $T_f = 1/f$.
- **Diffusive timescale:** $\tau = L^2/D$ (the characteristic time for Ag⁺ to diffuse across the channel of length $L$).

Then
$$N_{1/e} = \frac{fL^2}{D} = \frac{L^2/D}{1/f} = \frac{\tau}{T_f}.$$

Thus $N_{1/e}$ is the ratio of the diffusive timescale $\tau = L^2/D$ to the pulse period $1/f$: it counts how many pulse periods fit within one diffusive relaxation time. When $N_{1/e} \gg 1$ (i.e., $f\tau \gg 1$), many pulses are needed to wash out a perturbation, meaning the device has long memory persistence. When $N_{1/e} \ll 1$ (i.e., $f\tau \ll 1$), the perturbation decays well within a single inter-pulse interval, meaning the device resets rapidly between pulses.

最终答案：$$\boxed{N_{1/e} = \dfrac{fL^2}{D}}$$

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
In the planar 2D channel memristor (PTCM), the Ag:GST mixed ionic-electronic conductor (MIEC) reservoir is coupled to a monolayer MoS₂ semiconductor channel. Upon removal of an applied bias, Ag⁺ ions that have entered the MoS₂ channel undergo spontaneous back-diffusion along the channel toward the MIEC reservoir boundary, which acts as a perfect sink fixing the Ag⁺ concentration at zero there. This back-diffusion process sets the device forgetting timescale τ.

Let L denote the effective diffusion path length along the channel, and let D denote the effective Ag⁺ diffusion coefficient in the monolayer MoS₂ channel.

Derive a closed-form symbolic expression for τ exclusively in terms of L and D, retaining only leading-order scaling and omitting prefactors of order unity. Express your answer as $\boxed{\tau = \ldots}$.
output:
## 解答

**S1 — Identify the governing physics from the previous step.**

From the previous step, the forgetting timescale τ of the PTCM is governed by the spontaneous back-diffusion of Ag⁺ ions from the interior of the MoS₂ channel to the Ag:GST MIEC reservoir boundary. This is a diffusion problem characterized by:
- a diffusion coefficient D (effective Ag⁺ diffusivity in monolayer MoS₂),
- a characteristic length L (the diffusion path length from the channel interior to the MIEC reservoir boundary),
- a perfect-sink boundary condition at the reservoir (Ag⁺ concentration = 0 there).

The quasi-2D geometry of monolayer MoS₂ (thickness ≪ L) justifies treating the diffusion as effectively one-dimensional along L.

**S2 — Apply the standard diffusive timescale relation.**

The governing equation for the Ag⁺ concentration c(x, t) in the 1D channel is:

∂c/∂t = D ∂²c/∂x²

To extract the characteristic timescale, balance the orders of magnitude of each term:
- Left-hand side (time-derivative term): ∂c/∂t ~ c/τ
- Right-hand side (spatial-derivative term): D ∂²c/∂x² ~ D · c/L²

Setting these equal:

c/τ ~ D · c/L²

**S3 — Solve for τ.**

Dividing both sides by c (assumed nonzero) and rearranging:

τ ~ L²/D

Dropping the order-unity prefactor (as prescribed by the leading-order scaling requirement), the forgetting timescale is:

τ = L²/D

This is the standard Einstein diffusive timescale. Physically, a longer channel (larger L) or a slower Ag⁺ diffusivity (smaller D) both increase τ, meaning the device retains its potentiated conductance state for longer—consistent with the biological analogy where slower Ca²⁺ clearance extends synaptic memory.

最终答案：\boxed{\tau = \dfrac{L^{2}}{D}}

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
In the planar 2D channel memristor (PTCM), an Ag:GST mixed ionic-electronic conductor (MIEC) reservoir is coupled to a monolayer MoS₂ semiconductor channel. Upon bias removal, solubility contrast drives spontaneous Ag⁺ back-diffusion from the MoS₂ channel to the reservoir. The back-diffusion is governed by one-dimensional diffusion along the channel length $L$ with effective diffusion coefficient $D$ in monolayer MoS₂; the MIEC reservoir boundary acts as a perfect sink.

Under periodic stimulation at frequency $f$, each voltage pulse of width $\Delta t$ instantaneously injects a Ag⁺ increment $\alpha\,\Delta t$ into the MoS₂ channel ($\alpha$ is a dimensionless amplitude-dependent injection rate). Between pulses, excess Ag⁺ decays exponentially with the diffusive forgetting timescale $\tau$, giving the discrete-time map
$$c_{n+1} = (c_n + \alpha\,\Delta t)\,e^{-1/(f\tau)}.$$

Determine the stability multiplier $\lambda$ of the unique non-trivial fixed point of this map, expressed solely in terms of $D$, $f$, and $L$, and provide your answer as $\boxed{\cdots}$.
output:
## 解答

**S1 — Substitute the perturbation ansatz into the map.**

Write $c_n = c^* + \delta_n$. Substituting into the map $c_{n+1} = (c_n + \alpha\,\Delta t)\,e^{-D/(fL^2)}$ gives
$$c^* + \delta_{n+1} = \bigl(c^* + \delta_n + \alpha\,\Delta t\bigr)\,e^{-D/(fL^2)}.$$

**S2 — Apply the fixed-point identity to cancel $c^*$ terms.**

By definition of the fixed point, $c^*$ satisfies
$$c^* = (c^* + \alpha\,\Delta t)\,e^{-D/(fL^2)}.$$
Subtracting this identity from the equation in S1:
$$\delta_{n+1} = \delta_n\,e^{-D/(fL^2)}.$$
This is exact to all orders in $\delta_n$ (the map is affine, so the linearization is exact).

**S3 — Identify the stability multiplier.**

The linearized recurrence $\delta_{n+1} = \lambda\,\delta_n$ has multiplier
$$\lambda = e^{-D/(fL^2)}.$$
This expression involves only $D$, $f$, and $L$, with no occurrence of $\tau$, consistent with the substitution $\tau = L^2/D$ already incorporated in the map.

**S4 — Verify the stability criterion.**

The fixed point is linearly stable iff $|\lambda| < 1$. Since $\lambda = e^{-D/(fL^2)}$ is real and positive, the condition reduces to $\lambda < 1$, i.e.,
$$e^{-D/(fL^2)} < 1.$$
This holds if and only if $-D/(fL^2) < 0$, which is guaranteed for all $D > 0$, $f > 0$, $L > 0$. The stability criterion is therefore unconditionally satisfied for all physically admissible parameter values.

**S5 — Physical interpretation.**

The multiplier $\lambda = e^{-D/(fL^2)}$ is the per-cycle geometric contraction factor. Any perturbation $\delta_n$ decays as $\delta_n = \lambda^n \delta_0 \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, confirming that $c^*$ is a globally attracting fixed point of the (affine, hence linear) dynamics. The same exponential factor that governs diffusive clearance of Ag⁺ in the channel also governs the rate at which transient deviations from steady state are suppressed.

最终答案：$$\boxed{\lambda = e^{-D/(fL^2)}}$$
with stability criterion $\lambda < 1$, satisfied for all $D > 0$, $f > 0$, $L > 0$.

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
An abrupt p-n homojunction is formed within a single MAPbI\(_3\) perovskite absorber layer. In MAPbI\(_3\), the Kröger–Vink defect charge convention assigns iodine vacancies (V\(_I\)) and methylammonium interstitials (MA\(_i\)) as donors, while lead vacancies (V\(_{Pb}\)) and lead antisites (Pb\(_{MA}\)) act as acceptors. I-poor / Pb-rich deposition conditions lower the formation energy of donor defects, producing an n-type region of uniform donor density \(N_D\); I-rich / Pb-poor conditions lower the formation energy of acceptor defects, producing a p-type region of uniform acceptor density \(N_A\). The built-in potential satisfies \(q\,V_{\mathrm{bi}} = E_F^n - E_F^p\) with \(q > 0\) the elementary charge; the thermal voltage is \(V_T = k_BT/q\); \(n_i\) is the intrinsic carrier concentration; and \(\varepsilon\) is the permittivity of the perovskite. The junction is abrupt, all donors and acceptors are fully ionised, free-carrier density is zero inside the depletion region, the system is in full thermal equilibrium at zero applied bias, and the electric field vanishes exactly at the outer edges of the depletion region on both sides.

Derive a single closed-form expression for the peak electric-field magnitude \(|E_{\mathrm{max}}|\) at the metallurgical junction, expressed solely in terms of \(\varepsilon\), \(q\), \(V_{\mathrm{bi}}\), \(N_A\), and \(N_D\), and write your final answer as \(|E_{\mathrm{max}}| = \boxed{\cdots}\).
output:
## 解答

**S1. Recall the depletion-width results from the previous step.**

The total depletion width and the individual side widths are
$$W = \sqrt{\frac{2\varepsilon V_{\mathrm{bi}}(N_A+N_D)}{qN_AN_D}},$$
$$x_n = \frac{N_A}{N_A+N_D}\,W = \sqrt{\frac{2\varepsilon V_{\mathrm{bi}}}{q}\cdot\frac{N_A}{N_D(N_A+N_D)}},$$
$$x_p = \frac{N_D}{N_A+N_D}\,W = \sqrt{\frac{2\varepsilon V_{\mathrm{bi}}}{q}\cdot\frac{N_D}{N_A(N_A+N_D)}},$$
with the charge-neutrality condition $N_D x_n = N_A x_p$.

**S2. Integrate Poisson's equation on the n-side.**

Inside the n-side depletion region ($0 \le x \le x_n$), the only charge is the ionised donor charge, so Poisson's equation gives
$$\frac{dE}{dx} = \frac{qN_D}{\varepsilon}.$$
Integrating from an arbitrary point $x$ to the outer edge $x_n$ and applying $E(x_n) = 0$:
$$E(x_n) - E(x) = \frac{qN_D}{\varepsilon}(x_n - x) \implies E(x) = -\frac{qN_D}{\varepsilon}(x_n - x), \quad 0 \le x \le x_n.$$
The field is negative (directed from n toward p), consistent with the built-in field direction.

**S3. Evaluate the peak field at the metallurgical junction.**

Setting $x = 0$:
$$E(0) = -\frac{qN_D\,x_n}{\varepsilon}, \qquad |E_{\max}| = \frac{qN_D\,x_n}{\varepsilon}.$$

**S4. Substitute $x_n$ to obtain the fully expanded closed form.**

Substituting the expression for $x_n$ from S1:
$$|E_{\max}| = \frac{qN_D}{\varepsilon}\sqrt{\frac{2\varepsilon V_{\mathrm{bi}}}{q}\cdot\frac{N_A}{N_D(N_A+N_D)}} = \sqrt{\frac{2qV_{\mathrm{bi}}N_AN_D}{\varepsilon(N_A+N_D)}}.$$

**S5. Verify the geometric relation $|E_{\max}| = 2V_{\mathrm{bi}}/W$.**

The electric-field profile is linear (triangular) on each side of the junction. The total built-in potential equals the area under the $|E(x)|$ triangle over the full depletion width:
$$V_{\mathrm{bi}} = \frac{1}{2}|E_{\max}|\,(x_n + x_p) = \frac{1}{2}|E_{\max}|\,W.$$
Solving:
$$|E_{\max}| = \frac{2V_{\mathrm{bi}}}{W}.$$

**S6. Verify the form $|E_{\max}| = qN_AN_DW/(\varepsilon(N_A+N_D))$.**

Squaring $W$ and rearranging:
$$W^2 = \frac{2\varepsilon V_{\mathrm{bi}}(N_A+N_D)}{qN_AN_D} \implies V_{\mathrm{bi}} = \frac{qN_AN_D\,W^2}{2\varepsilon(N_A+N_D)}.$$
Substituting into $|E_{\max}| = 2V_{\mathrm{bi}}/W$:
$$|E_{\max}| = \frac{2}{W}\cdot\frac{qN_AN_D\,W^2}{2\varepsilon(N_A+N_D)} = \frac{qN_AN_D\,W}{\varepsilon(N_A+N_D)}.$$

**S7. Consistency check from the p-side.**

By symmetry, integrating Poisson's equation on the p-side with charge density $-qN_A$ and boundary condition $E(-x_p)=0$ gives $|E_{\max}| = qN_A x_p/\varepsilon$. Using $N_Ax_p = N_Dx_n$ (charge neutrality), this equals $qN_Dx_n/\varepsilon$, confirming the result of S3.

**Conclusion.** All three forms are equivalent:
$$|E_{\max}| = \frac{2V_{\mathrm{bi}}}{W} = \frac{qN_AN_D\,W}{\varepsilon(N_A+N_D)} = \sqrt{\frac{2qV_{\mathrm{bi}}N_AN_D}{\varepsilon(N_A+N_D)}}.$$

最终答案：$$\boxed{|E_{\max}| = \frac{2\,V_{\mathrm{bi}}}{W} = \frac{q\,N_A\,N_D\,W}{\varepsilon\,(N_A+N_D)} = \sqrt{\frac{2\,q\,V_{\mathrm{bi}}\,N_A\,N_D}{\varepsilon\,(N_A+N_D)}}}$$

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
In the organometallic halide perovskite MAPbI₃, the conductivity type of a thin film is controlled by the chemical potential environment during deposition. Under I-poor / Pb-rich precursor conditions, iodine vacancies (V_I, effective positive charge → donor) and methylammonium interstitials (MA_i, donates electrons → donor) have low formation energies, producing an n-type region with donor density $N_D$ and pre-contact Fermi level $E_F^n$. Under I-rich / Pb-poor conditions, lead vacancies (V_Pb, effective negative charge → acceptor) and related acceptor defects have low formation energies, producing a p-type region with acceptor density $N_A$ and pre-contact Fermi level $E_F^p$. When these two regions are brought into contact to form a p-n homojunction, a built-in potential $V_{\mathrm{bi}}$ develops at thermal equilibrium, defined by $q\,V_{\mathrm{bi}} = E_F^n - E_F^p$ where $q > 0$ is the elementary charge. The thermal voltage is $V_T = k_B T / q$ and $n_i$ is the intrinsic carrier concentration.

Derive a closed-form expression for $V_{\mathrm{bi}}$ and express your answer in a single $\boxed{\cdots}$ in terms of $V_T$, $N_A$, $N_D$, and $n_i$ only.
output:
## 解答

**S1 – Write the pre-contact Fermi level on the n-side relative to $E_i$.**

Under complete ionisation and thermal equilibrium, the electron density on the n-side satisfies $n = N_D$, so
$$E_F^n - E_i = k_B T \ln\!\left(\frac{N_D}{n_i}\right) = q V_T \ln\!\left(\frac{N_D}{n_i}\right).$$

**S2 – Write the pre-contact Fermi level on the p-side relative to $E_i$.**

Similarly, with $p = N_A$ on the p-side,
$$E_i - E_F^p = k_B T \ln\!\left(\frac{N_A}{n_i}\right) = q V_T \ln\!\left(\frac{N_A}{n_i}\right),$$
which rearranges to
$$E_F^p - E_i = -q V_T \ln\!\left(\frac{N_A}{n_i}\right).$$

**S3 – Compute the pre-contact Fermi-level separation.**

$$E_F^n - E_F^p = \bigl(E_F^n - E_i\bigr) - \bigl(E_F^p - E_i\bigr)
= q V_T \ln\!\left(\frac{N_D}{n_i}\right) + q V_T \ln\!\left(\frac{N_A}{n_i}\right).$$

Combining the logarithms:
$$E_F^n - E_F^p = q V_T \ln\!\left(\frac{N_D}{n_i} \cdot \frac{N_A}{n_i}\right) = q V_T \ln\!\left(\frac{N_A N_D}{n_i^2}\right).$$

**S4 – Divide by $q$ to obtain $V_{\mathrm{bi}}$.**

Using the sign convention $q\,V_{\mathrm{bi}} = E_F^n - E_F^p$:
$$V_{\mathrm{bi}} = \frac{E_F^n - E_F^p}{q} = V_T \ln\!\left(\frac{N_A N_D}{n_i^2}\right).$$

Since $N_A N_D > n_i^2$ in a doped semiconductor, $V_{\mathrm{bi}} > 0$ as required by the sign convention.

最终答案：$$\boxed{V_{\mathrm{bi}} = V_T \ln\!\left(\dfrac{N_A\, N_D}{n_i^{2}}\right)}$$

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
Phasor analysis projects a time-domain signal $I(t)$ onto sine and cosine basis functions at modulation frequency $\omega > 0$, yielding coordinates
$$g = \frac{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} I(t)\cos(\omega t)\,dt}{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} I(t)\,dt}, \qquad s = \frac{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} I(t)\sin(\omega t)\,dt}{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} I(t)\,dt}.$$
For a single-exponential decay $I(t) = e^{-t/\tau}$ ($t \geq 0$, $\tau > 0$, $\omega > 0$), let $P_i = (g_i, s_i)$ denote the phasor coordinates of the component with lifetime $\tau_i$ ($i = 1, 2$).

Consider the bi-exponential signal
$$I(t) = A\,e^{-t/\tau_1} + (1-A)\,e^{-t/\tau_2}, \quad t \geq 0,$$
where $0 < A < 1$, $\tau_1 > 0$, $\tau_2 > 0$, $\tau_1 \neq \tau_2$, and $\omega > 0$. Its phasor coordinates are $(g_{\mathrm{mix}}, s_{\mathrm{mix}})$ as defined by the normalized Fourier transforms above. Define
$$w = \frac{A\tau_1}{A\tau_1 + (1-A)\tau_2}.
$$

Derive a closed-form expression for $\Delta = g_{\mathrm{mix}} - (g_{\mathrm{mix}}^2 + s_{\mathrm{mix}}^2)$, prove that $\Delta > 0$ strictly whenever $\tau_1 \neq \tau_2$ and $0 < w < 1$, and express your final answer for $\Delta$ in a $\boxed{\cdots}$, in terms of $\{w, g_1, g_2, s_1, s_2\}$.
output:
## 解答

**S1 – Expand $g_{\mathrm{mix}}^2 + s_{\mathrm{mix}}^2$.**

Using the convex-combination representations:
$$g_{\mathrm{mix}}^2 = \bigl[w\,g_1+(1-w)g_2\bigr]^2 = w^2 g_1^2 + 2w(1-w)g_1 g_2 + (1-w)^2 g_2^2,$$
$$s_{\mathrm{mix}}^2 = \bigl[w\,s_1+(1-w)s_2\bigr]^2 = w^2 s_1^2 + 2w(1-w)s_1 s_2 + (1-w)^2 s_2^2.$$
Summing:
$$g_{\mathrm{mix}}^2+s_{\mathrm{mix}}^2 = w^2(g_1^2+s_1^2) + 2w(1-w)(g_1 g_2+s_1 s_2) + (1-w)^2(g_2^2+s_2^2).$$

**S2 – Apply the semicircle identity $g_i^2+s_i^2=g_i$.**

Substituting $g_1^2+s_1^2=g_1$ and $g_2^2+s_2^2=g_2$:
$$g_{\mathrm{mix}}^2+s_{\mathrm{mix}}^2 = w^2 g_1 + 2w(1-w)(g_1 g_2+s_1 s_2) + (1-w)^2 g_2.$$

**S3 – Write $g_{\mathrm{mix}}$ and form the deficit $\Delta$.**

$$g_{\mathrm{mix}} = w\,g_1+(1-w)g_2.$$
$$\Delta = g_{\mathrm{mix}}-(g_{\mathrm{mix}}^2+s_{\mathrm{mix}}^2)
= \bigl[w\,g_1+(1-w)g_2\bigr] - \bigl[w^2 g_1 + 2w(1-w)(g_1 g_2+s_1 s_2)+(1-w)^2 g_2\bigr].$$

**S4 – Collect coefficients.**

Coefficient of $g_1$: $w - w^2 = w(1-w)$.
Coefficient of $g_2$: $(1-w)-(1-w)^2 = w(1-w)$.
Remaining cross term: $-2w(1-w)(g_1 g_2+s_1 s_2)$.

Hence:
$$\Delta = w(1-w)\bigl[g_1+g_2 - 2(g_1 g_2+s_1 s_2)\bigr].$$

**S5 – Re-apply the semicircle identity to simplify $g_1+g_2$.**

Since $g_i = g_i^2+s_i^2$, we have $g_1+g_2 = (g_1^2+s_1^2)+(g_2^2+s_2^2)$. Therefore:
$$g_1+g_2 - 2(g_1 g_2+s_1 s_2) = (g_1^2+s_1^2)+(g_2^2+s_2^2)-2g_1 g_2 - 2s_1 s_2
= (g_1-g_2)^2+(s_1-s_2)^2.$$

Thus:
$$\boxed{\Delta = w(1-w)\bigl[(g_1-g_2)^2+(s_1-s_2)^2\bigr].}$$

**S6 – Strict positivity argument.**

- **Factor $w(1-w)>0$:** Since $0<w<1$, both $w>0$ and $1-w>0$, so $w(1-w)>0$.
- **Factor $(g_1-g_2)^2+(s_1-s_2)^2>0$:** For fixed $\omega>0$, the map $\tau\mapsto\bigl(1/(1+\omega^2\tau^2),\;\omega\tau/(1+\omega^2\tau^2)\bigr)$ is injective on $(0,\infty)$ (both $g$ and $s$ are smooth functions of $\tau$ that uniquely determine $\omega^2\tau^2$ from $s/g=\omega\tau$, so $\tau_1\neq\tau_2$ implies $(g_1,s_1)\neq(g_2,s_2)$). Therefore $(g_1-g_2)^2+(s_1-s_2)^2>0$.

Combining both factors, $\Delta>0$, which proves that $(g_{\mathrm{mix}},s_{\mathrm{mix}})$ lies **strictly inside** the universal semicircle $g^2+s^2=g$ whenever $\tau_1\neq\tau_2$ and $0<w<1$.

最终答案：\boxed{\Delta = g_{\mathrm{mix}} - \bigl(g_{\mathrm{mix}}^2+s_{\mathrm{mix}}^2\bigr) = w(1-w)\bigl[(g_1-g_2)^2+(s_1-s_2)^2\bigr] > 0}

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
Phasor analysis projects a time-domain intensity signal $I(t)$ onto sine and cosine basis functions at modulation frequency $\omega > 0$, yielding coordinates
$$g = \frac{\int I(t)\cos(\omega t)\,dt}{\int I(t)\,dt}, \qquad s = \frac{\int I(t)\sin(\omega t)\,dt}{\int I(t)\,dt}.$$
For a single-exponential decay $I(t) = e^{-t/\tau}$ ($t \geq 0$, $\tau > 0$), the phasor point $(g, s)$ lies on the universal semicircle $g^2 + s^2 = g$.

Consider a bi-exponential signal $I(t) = A\,e^{-t/\tau_1} + (1-A)\,e^{-t/\tau_2}$ ($t \geq 0$, $0 < A < 1$, $\tau_1 \neq \tau_2$, $\tau_1, \tau_2 > 0$, $\omega > 0$). Let $(g_1, s_1)$ and $(g_2, s_2)$ be the phasor coordinates of the individual components with lifetimes $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$, let $(g_{\mathrm{mix}}, s_{\mathrm{mix}})$ be the phasor of the full bi-exponential signal, let
$$w = \frac{A\tau_1}{A\tau_1 + (1-A)\tau_2} \in (0,1),$$
and let $\Delta = g_{\mathrm{mix}} - (g_{\mathrm{mix}}^2 + s_{\mathrm{mix}}^2)$.

Express the squared Euclidean chord length $D^2 = (g_1 - g_2)^2 + (s_1 - s_2)^2$ in the form $\boxed{\cdots}$ in terms of $\Delta$ and $w$ only.
output:
## 解答

**S1 — Recall the deficit identity (from the previous step).**

The established result is
$$
\Delta = w(1-w)\,D^2, \qquad D^2 = (g_1-g_2)^2+(s_1-s_2)^2.
$$
This holds for any bi-exponential mixture phasor with intensity-weighted fraction $w\in(0,1)$ and single-exponential endpoints on the universal semicircle $g^2+s^2=g$.

---

**S2 — Part (a): Invert the deficit identity.**

Since $w\in(0,1)$ strictly, we have $w(1-w)>0$. Dividing both sides of $\Delta = w(1-w)\,D^2$ by $w(1-w)$ gives
$$
D^2 = \frac{\Delta}{w(1-w)}.
$$
This is an *exact equality*: any bi-exponential decomposition with weight $w$ that is consistent with deficit $\Delta$ must have its two endpoint phasors separated by squared Euclidean distance exactly $\Delta/[w(1-w)]$. It is not a lower bound; the deficit identity is an equality, so $D^2$ is uniquely determined by $\{\Delta, w\}$.

---

**S3 — Part (b): Complete system of locus constraints.**

For the endpoint pair $(g_1,s_1),(g_2,s_2)$ to be consistent with the measured data $(g_{\mathrm{mix}},s_{\mathrm{mix}},\Delta)$ and weight $w$, three groups of constraints must hold simultaneously:

**Constraint 1 — Semicircle membership** (two equations):
$$
g_1^2 + s_1^2 = g_1, \qquad g_2^2 + s_2^2 = g_2.
$$

**Constraint 2 — Convex-combination (centroid) conditions** (two equations):
$$
w\,g_1 + (1-w)\,g_2 = g_{\mathrm{mix}}, \qquad w\,s_1 + (1-w)\,s_2 = s_{\mathrm{mix}}.
$$

**Constraint 3 — Chord-length consistency** (one equation):
$$
(g_1-g_2)^2 + (s_1-s_2)^2 = \frac{\Delta}{w(1-w)}.
$$

**Dependence note:** Constraint 3 is *not independent* of Constraints 1 and 2. It follows algebraically from them via the deficit identity derived in the previous step: substituting Constraints 1 and 2 into $\Delta = g_{\mathrm{mix}}-(g_{\mathrm{mix}}^2+s_{\mathrm{mix}}^2)$ and expanding recovers $\Delta = w(1-w)\,D^2$, which is exactly Constraint 3. Stating Constraint 3 is required for completeness and to make the required endpoint separation explicit, but it carries no additional information beyond Constraints 1 and 2.

**Locus characterization:** Constraints 1 and 2 constitute four equations in four unknowns $(g_1,s_1,g_2,s_2)$. For generic $(g_{\mathrm{mix}},s_{\mathrm{mix}},w)$ with $(g_{\mathrm{mix}},s_{\mathrm{mix}})$ strictly inside the semicircle (i.e., $\Delta>0$), this system has a generically finite (discrete) set of solutions, related pairwise by the label swap $P_1\leftrightarrow P_2$ with $w\leftrightarrow 1-w$. The locus of valid endpoint pairs is therefore the finite set of ordered pairs $(P_1,P_2)$ on the curve $g^2+s^2=g$ satisfying
$$
w\,P_1+(1-w)\,P_2=(g_{\mathrm{mix}},s_{\mathrm{mix}})
\quad\text{and}\quad
|P_1-P_2|^2=\frac{\Delta}{w(1-w)}.
$$

最终答案：\boxed{D^2 = \dfrac{\Delta}{w(1-w)}}

instruction: 请解答以下问题，并给出详细推导或分析过程：
input:
A directed graph G is defined over the node set {CSE, SI, SF, PEOU, ATT}. CSE, SI, and SF are external variables. PEOU is the sole eligible intermediate internal construct. ATT is the terminal node and is never used as an intermediate in any path. The edges of G are:
  { CSE→PEOU,  SI→PEOU,  SF→ATT,  SF→PEOU,  PEOU→ATT }

Definitions:
- A **direct path** from external variable X to ATT is a single directed edge X→ATT (path length = 1).
- An **indirect path** from X to ATT is a directed path of length ≥ 2 that passes through PEOU as the intermediate internal construct.
- **Full mediation**: X has at least one indirect path to ATT through PEOU, and no direct edge X→ATT exists in G.
- **Partial mediation**: X has at least one indirect path to ATT through PEOU, and a direct edge X→ATT also exists in G.
- **No mediation**: X has no indirect path to ATT through any internal construct.
- **Path-reach classification** (mutually exclusive and exhaustive for variables that reach ATT): *Direct-only* (at least one direct path, no indirect path); *Indirect-only* (at least one indirect path, no direct path); *Both* (at least one direct path and at least one indirect path).
- Two paths are distinct if and only if they differ in at least one directed edge. All edges are strictly unidirectional; reverse traversal is not permitted.

Identify the unique external variable in {CSE, SI, SF} that exhibits partial mediation in G, and express your answer as a structured symbolic triple:
  (i) the partial-mediation variable and its mediation type,
  (ii) its direct path (as a directed edge sequence using →),
  (iii) its indirect path (as a directed edge sequence using →),
using only the symbols {CSE, SI, SF, PEOU, ATT} and the arrow operator →, wrapped in \boxed{...}.
output:
## 解答

S1 (Reconstruct the working graph). The five-edge graph for this step is fixed as:
  G = { CSE→PEOU, SI→PEOU, SF→ATT, SF→PEOU, PEOU→ATT }.
Edges present: CSE→PEOU ✓, SI→PEOU ✓, SF→ATT ✓, SF→PEOU ✓, PEOU→ATT ✓.
Edges absent (relevant): CSE→ATT ✗, SI→ATT ✗.

S2 (Enumerate all directed paths from CSE to ATT).
  - Direct path (length 1): requires edge CSE→ATT. This edge is not in G. → None.
  - Indirect path (length ≥ 2 through PEOU): CSE→PEOU (edge present) then PEOU→ATT (edge present). Path: CSE→PEOU→ATT. ✓
  - No other paths exist (no other out-edges from CSE in G).
  Result: one indirect path CSE→PEOU→ATT; no direct path.
  Path-reach: Indirect-only. Mediation: Full mediation (indirect path exists, no direct edge CSE→ATT).

S3 (Enumerate all directed paths from SI to ATT).
  - Direct path (length 1): requires edge SI→ATT. This edge is not in G. → None.
  - Indirect path (length ≥ 2 through PEOU): SI→PEOU (edge present) then PEOU→ATT (edge present). Path: SI→PEOU→ATT. ✓
  - No other paths exist (no other out-edges from SI in G).
  Result: one indirect path SI→PEOU→ATT; no direct path.
  Path-reach: Indirect-only. Mediation: Full mediation (indirect path exists, no direct edge SI→ATT).

S4 (Enumerate all directed paths from SF to ATT).
  - Direct path (length 1): requires edge SF→ATT. This edge IS in G. Path: SF→ATT. ✓
  - Indirect path (length ≥ 2 through PEOU): SF→PEOU (edge present) then PEOU→ATT (edge present). Path: SF→PEOU→ATT. ✓
  - No other indirect paths exist (PEOU has no out-edge other than PEOU→ATT in G).
  Result: one direct path SF→ATT; one indirect path SF→PEOU→ATT.
